design: Phase III randomised double-blind placebo-controlled comparison of capivasertib plus fulvestrant versus placebo plus fulvestrant.
population: HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer after progression during or after aromatase-inhibitor treatment, with or without a CDK4/6 inhibitor. The trial enrolled 708 patients; the PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered population comprised 289 (155 versus 134). NCCP00947 is restricted to the qualifying altered population.
clinical_takeaway: The combination improved progression-free survival in the biomarker-altered group. Final overall survival in 2026 was not significantly improved; do not claim a demonstrated survival advantage or retain an outdated OS-immature label.

outcomes.interpretation: Dual primary endpoint met. The median is a group summary, not a prediction for an individual.

outcomes.analysis: Final analysis; ESMO Breast 2026 abstract 417O, ESMO Open 11(suppl 4):107440
outcomes.interpretation: Not statistically significant. Do not claim a survival gain, and do not interpret the numerically different medians as proof of harm or a precise expected lifespan.

context_only.all_comer_pfs: The original overall population also met the PFS endpoint, but this does not expand the NCCP indication beyond qualifying alterations.
context_only.overall_os: The final abstract reports overall-population OS HR 1.00 (95% CI 0.83–1.19); this provides no established survival advantage. The clinician card should lead with the indicated altered population.

limitations: Placebo plus fulvestrant is the trial comparator; there is no head-to-head basis here to rank capivasertib against other modern targeted/endocrine regimens.
Final OS is a secondary endpoint and was not significantly improved. The final source is a congress abstract, distinct from the 2023 full primary PFS report.
The trial enrolled ECOG 0–1, while NCCP eligibility extends to 0–2; evidence is less direct for performance status 2.
Type 1 diabetes, Type 2 diabetes requiring insulin and HbA1c >8% were not studied; do not treat this evidence gap as an invented absolute NCCP exclusion.
Do not blend the unselected trial population with the indicated altered subgroup, or give these numerical outcome estimates on patient-facing guides.

primary_sources.title: Turner NC et al. Capivasertib in Hormone Receptor-Positive Advanced Breast Cancer. NEJM 2023;388:2058–2070.
primary_sources.status: Primary randomised trial report; data also verified in current EMA Truqap section 5.1.

retrieval_note: The official ESMO Open search index exposes altered-population medians 28.5/30.4, HR 0.83 (0.63–1.10), P=.201 and the conclusion that OS was not significantly improved. A visual reproduction of the original trial result table in public ResearchToPractice slides page 89 corroborates these numbers but is not used as the primary evidence citation.
